added: # The seven shortest centre fields among the venues that hosted regular-season
# games (MLB venue endpoint, fieldInfo.center): Oracle Park 391 ft, Dodger

commits.subject: Coverage, breadth again: `short-centre-fields`, the venue surface's ORTHOGONAL dimension. Left line and centre field pick out different parks — Fenway Park is short to left (310 ft) and deep to centre (420) — so this slice is the seven shortest centre fields in MLB's venue data, a park set the corpus had never covered: Oracle Park 391 ft (the league's shortest), Dodger Stadium 395, Angel Stadium 396, Petco Park 396, PNC Park 399, Rate Field 400 and Wrigley Field 400. Twelve games, one per date, every date previously unused. Each feed was verified before wiring: 3,692 tracked pitches, ZERO pitches missing tracking coordinates, 24 home runs, and a maximum plate-crossing deviation of 0.0011 ft against the 0.01 budget. Slice numbers from the built Arrow: 1,752 swings, 420 whiffs (24.0%), 600 pitches with measured contact, 80 pitchers, 154 batters, 11 pitch types. TWO PROCESS CATCHES worth recording. (1) The picking bug: my first pass produced five of twelve games at PNC Park and OMITTED ORACLE PARK ENTIRELY — the league's shortest centre field, missing from a slice whose whole criterion is centre fields. Fixed by taking one game per park first (rarest park first, so every park in the criterion gets in) and only then filling by date: the lesson is that a criterion-based pick must be checked to include the criterion's extreme. (2) A wiring slip: my card-insert replacement swallowed the PREVIOUS card's closing brace, and tsc caught it immediately — the gates earned their keep. A MEASUREMENT NEAR-MISS worth recording too: the built slice's play_event == "Home Run" pitch count is 75 while the RUN count is 24, because play_event repeats the appearance's outcome on every pitch of it, exactly as designed; the card therefore states 24 home runs (the run count), and a pitch count there would have been wrong — the column's semantics paying off in the act of writing the card. DETERMINISTIC RESULTS: coverage_index 63.512376 -> 63.911279 (+0.63%); corpus 51,949 -> 55,641 pitches, games and dates 173 -> 185, pitchers 627 -> 644, batters 681 -> 692, scenarios 30 -> 31. Gates: pytest 460 (the scenario parametrisation re-checked EVERY slice's row count), vitest 363, tsc, production build, parity 55,641/55,641; browser check shows the caption with all seven verified dimensions, 3,687 of 3,692 shown, 24.0% whiff, 3,692 rows, 12 game days and no console errors. The score reading (71,603) is the highest of the recent window and is host noise — the throughputs read 1,055/1,190 — and is not treated as evidence about this change.

added: # Twelve games decided by nine runs or more, four per season and one per date
# (179 runs in all, margins 9-16). Four of them had an arm that never topped

commits.subject: Coverage: new blowouts slice — twelve games decided by nine runs or more, four per season and one per date (margins 9 to 16, 179 runs in all: 18-7 in Boston, 17-1 in San Francisco, 17-2 in Arizona, 11-1 and 16-1 in Tampa Bay). Candidates came from the schedule with `hydrate=linescore` (one request per date, nine innings, margin >= 9), then each feed was verified for the margin, the innings and the plate-crossing invariant — and per pitcher for the top speed, which found that FOUR of the twelve had an arm that never topped 75 mph as the game ran away, the slowest a 43.8 mph pitch (James McCann) with Atlanta 17 runs ahead in Arizona, and a 62.0 mph one from Tyler Fitzgerald (a CF pitching, per the box score's position list). 3,680 pitches, 1,732 swings, 338 whiffs, 723 with measured contact. Corpus 34,673→38,353 pitches, 115→127 games and dates, 525→553 pitchers, 635→650 batters, 25→26 scenarios; coverage_index 60.85→61.44 (+0.59 points, +0.97%, matching the predicted log2 delta). THE COVERAGE-VERSUS-TAX QUESTION IS NOW OPEN AND MEASURED: three consecutive batches (runs 51-54) read below run 50's 82,583 even though each raised the index (+1.07%, +0.97%); per-pitch stage costs say the tree is fine (TS panels 5.82 → 5.93 across these two samples with a 6.45 outlier, python derive 10.32 → 10.38 µs/pitch, export flat per day-file), while per-run windows swing the python and panels stages by 2-8%. So each batch's +1% index is real and deterministic, but individual batches are no longer provable by the score in these windows — the suspicion of a mild superlinear heap tax remains unresolved. Two samples of this tree: 81,364 and 82,011 (at run 50's throughput level the index alone implies ~83,400). pytest 434, vitest 292, tsc, build, parity 38,353/38,353, all gates green.

added: # The six deepest centre fields among the venues that hosted regular-season
# games and whose centre distance the venue endpoint and the game feed AGREE on

commits.subject: Coverage, the counterpart to short-centre-fields: `deep-centre-fields`, the six deepest centre fields in MLB's venue data among parks hosting regular-season games — Fenway Park 420 ft, Comerica Park 420, Coors Field 415, Kauffman Stadium 410, Daikin Park (Minute Maid in 2024) 409 and Citi Field 408. Twelve games, one per date, all fresh dates; each feed verified first: 3,598 tracked pitches, ZERO missing coordinates, 37 home runs, max plate deviation 0.0010 ft. Slice numbers: 1,715 swings, 382 whiffs (22.3%), 633 with measured contact, 87 pitchers, 12 pitch types. A GENUINE DATA CONFLICT FOUND AND HANDLED: MLB's two endpoints disagree about Oriole Park at Camden Yards — the venue endpoint reports a 410 ft centre field and the game feed reports 400 for the same venue id — so a park whose value is not settled cannot be a criterion park for a distance theme. I added a CROSS-SOURCE CONSISTENCY GATE to the picker (keep only parks where the venue endpoint and the game feed agree) and Camden Yards is excluded and documented in the slice's own README row. AND A CLAIM CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING: I had written into the card "Coors Field is the highest ground in the majors at 5,280 ft" — altitude is not in the feed, which is precisely why I declined altitude as a criterion earlier in the session — so it was removed before the harness ran and the browser check confirms no "5,280" appears. A REPEATED MISTAKE, admitted: my card-insert replacement consumed the previous card's closing brace AGAIN (the same slip as run 81, whose lesson was already in the notes); tsc caught it immediately both times. The rule is now sharper: when inserting into an array literal, anchor on the array's END and include the preceding element's closing brace in the replacement. DETERMINISTIC RESULTS: coverage_index 63.951921 -> 64.319364 (+0.57%); corpus 55,641 -> 59,239 pitches, games and dates 185 -> 197, pitchers 644 -> 663, batters 692 -> 697, scenarios 31 -> 32. Gates: pytest 464 (the parametrisation re-checked every slice's row count), vitest 364, tsc, production build, parity 59,239/59,239; the browser shows the caption with all six verified dimensions, 3,589 of 3,598 shown, 22.3% whiff, 3,598 rows, 12 game days and no console errors. The score reading (71,728) is the same host-broken window and is not evidence about this change.

added: # The five shortest left-field lines among the venues that hosted regular-
# season games (MLB venue endpoint, fieldInfo.leftLine): Fenway Park 310 ft,

commits.subject: Coverage, reusing the venue surface found in run 71: the left-field LINE is the park dimension with the widest real spread in MLB's venue data (310-360 ft, 20 distinct values, versus 391-430 for centre), so `short-left-lines` takes twelve games at the five shortest lines among parks that actually hosted regular-season games — Fenway Park 310 ft, Tropicana Field 315, Minute Maid Park 315 (since renamed Daikin Park in the same venue id, visible by comparing the 2024 and 2025 feeds), Yankee Stadium 318 and Progressive Field 325. One game per date, and every one of the twelve dates was previously unused (checked against real_game_dates() before fetching). Each feed was verified before wiring: 3,576 tracked pitches, ZERO pitches with missing tracking coordinates, 29 home runs, and a maximum plate-crossing deviation of 0.0010 ft against the 0.01 budget. The slice's own numbers, computed from the built Arrow: 1,695 swings, 398 whiffs (23.5%) and 601 pitches with measured contact data. DETERMINISTIC RESULTS (host-independent): coverage_index 62.99 -> 63.38 (+0.63%), corpus 48,373 -> 51,949 pitches, games and dates 161 -> 173, pitchers 615 -> 627, batters 675 -> 681, scenarios 29 -> 30. The card states only measured facts — the dimensions and the counts — and deliberately does NOT call these parks hitter-friendly, because Oracle Park owns the league's shortest centre field (391 ft) and is famous for suppressing home runs. PROCESS: run 71's rule (assert every str.replace anchor count) held: all twelve wiring edits were asserted and all landed; the one defect that escaped was caught by the tsc gate instead (the spray VIEW is a preset layer, not a LensId). Gates: pytest 450, vitest 347, tsc, production build, parity 51,949/51,949; browser shows the card's stats (3,565 of 3,576 shown, 23.5% whiff, 3,576 rows, 12 game days) and its verified caption with no console errors. The score reading (63,230) is in the same host-broken window as runs 63-71 and is not evidence about this change; the deterministic index gain is the result.
